About Us

We are a Cairo team at NASA Space Apps. We turn technical errors into paths for exploration. We are building OrbitCraft, a simulator where players manage space missions, budgets, and cosmic anomalies using real NASA data and AI logic.
summary: StellarIS is a browser-based Space Mission Design Game that lets players plan and fly a complete mission to the Moon or Mars. Players choose an objective, design a spacecraft (instruments, engine, propellant, power system, antenna, shielding), pick a real launch vehicle, then watch the mission unfold with live telemetry and launch and landing scenes. Along the way they face random anomalies such as solar flares, power shortfalls and trajectory errors, and must choose between solutions that each cost mass, power, money or science. The simulation uses the rocket equation, orbital mechanics and published specifications of real launch vehicles and power systems. A final report explains why the mission succeeded or failed, so players learn that engineering is about trade-offs. This addresses the challenge by teaching complete mission design in a fun, replayable way. It matters because it turns hard aerospace concepts into decisions anyone can practice. Built with AI-assisted tools, then reviewed and tested by Team Atlantis 505.
details:
StellarIS is a browser-based Space Mission Design Game. Players pick one of four missions (Moon orbit, Moon landing, Mars orbit, Mars landing), design the spacecraft, and then fly it. They choose a launch vehicle (Electron, Falcon 9, Atlas V 551, Falcon Heavy), an engine (hydrazine, hypergolic, methane/oxygen or xenon ion), a power system (solar arrays or an MMRTG), science instruments, an antenna and radiation shielding. Live meters show launch mass, delta-v, power and budget. During flight the game simulates the rocket equation, Kepler orbits, sunlight falling with distance, radiation dose and radio delay, and pauses for random anomalies where the player must pick between solutions that each cost mass, power, money or science. A final report explains why the mission succeeded or failed and links the result to a real mission such as NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. The benefit is learning that engineering is a set of trade-offs. It is a single HTML, CSS and JavaScript file with canvas graphics, Web Audio and reduced-motion support. Part values are based on published specifications or approximated for game balance.

Use of SI: We used SI tools for ideation, research, coding and debugging, and writing. Manus generated the game code from our design specification, and Claude (Anthropic) helped us plan the design, write texts and review the work. The team directed the design, tested the game and checked the data.
